title: Min Jumps to End
statement:
Hop along a row of stepping stones and count the fewest hops needed to reach the last one.

Contract
- `reach` is a non-null, non-empty array of non-negative ints; `reach[i]` is the longest hop you may make forward from stone `i`, and you may hop any shorter distance (at least 1) too.
- You start on index 0 and want to stand on the last index. The last index is guaranteed to be reachable.
- Return the minimum number of hops; an array with one stone needs 0 hops.
- Do not mutate `reach`.

Examples
- `minJumps(new int[]{3, 1, 1, 2, 1, 4})` returns `2` (index 0 to 3, then to 5).
- `minJumps(new int[]{1, 1, 1, 1})` returns `3`.
- `minJumps(new int[]{5})` returns `0`.
hints: Hopping to the stone with the largest own value is not always best; what matters is how far you can get from the stone you land on.
Think in waves: all stones reachable with k hops form a window. The next window ends at the farthest point any stone in the current window can reach.
Scan once, tracking the end of the current window and the farthest reach seen; each time the scan hits the window end, count a hop. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space for n stones.
inputSyntax: Input: the hop lengths, where the last index is reachable, for example: [3, 1, 1, 2, 1, 4]
